executive_summary: The most serious problems are in the backend functions: a search endpoint that can be used to run arbitrary database commands, and task-update and profile-lookup endpoints that require no login and use an all-powerful database key. The database access rules also let users promote themselves to admin and read data that likely belongs to others. The front end renders comment text as raw HTML, which allows script injection that would run in other users' browsers. Remaining items are minor hardening issues.
overall_assessment:
The security posture is weak at the server edge. Several functions skip authentication and use privileged credentials, so database-level protections are bypassed entirely. The row-level policies are also loose in places, most importantly the self-service role change. The client-side XSS sink compounds the risk.

Fix the unauthenticated and injectable functions first, since they are directly exploitable by anyone. Then close the role escalation and XSS issues. Next, review the task, comment and project policies against the intended sharing model. Finally, clean up error messages, CORS and the demo configuration.
top_priorities: Parameterize the search-tasks query (no sql.unsafe) and use a least-privilege database role.
Require authentication in update-task and get-profile, verify ownership, whitelist updatable fields, and use the caller's JWT instead of the service-role key.
Prevent users from changing their own role (column-level grants or a trigger/WITH CHECK that keeps role unchanged).
Sanitize or stop using dangerouslySetInnerHTML for comment text.
Tighten tasks, comments and project_id policies to match the intended ownership model.

findings.title: SQL injection via string-interpolated search term in sql.unsafe
findings.evidence:
const query = `
      SELECT id, title, description, status
      FROM public.tasks
      WHERE title ILIKE '%${searchTerm}%'
      ORDER BY created_at DESC
      LIMIT 25
    `;

    const tasks = await sql.unsafe(query);
findings.description: The unauthenticated `q` query parameter is concatenated directly into a SQL string that is run via `sql.unsafe`. The connection uses DATABASE_URL, which is typically a privileged role that bypasses RLS.
findings.impact: An attacker can run arbitrary SQL, for example UNION-based extraction of any table or data modification, and fully compromise the database.
findings.remediation: Use parameterized queries with the tagged template, and escape LIKE wildcards if needed. Require authentication and run the query as a low-privilege role or through the user-scoped Supabase client so RLS applies. Cap the length of the search term.

findings.title: Unauthenticated update-task with service-role key and mass assignment (IDOR)
findings.description: The function performs no authentication or ownership check. It passes the client-supplied `changes` object straight into an update using the service-role key, which bypasses RLS.
findings.impact: Anyone can modify any task and any column, including owner_id, project_id and status, and so take over or tamper with other users' data.
findings.remediation: Verify the caller's JWT and derive the user from it. Check that the task belongs to that user, or use a client created with the caller's Authorization header so RLS applies. Allowlist and validate the updatable fields instead of passing the raw object.
findings.validation_notes: Check whether the function is deployed with verify_jwt enabled; even so, there is no ownership check.

findings.title: Stored XSS via dangerouslySetInnerHTML on comment text
findings.description: User-supplied comment text is rendered as raw HTML with no sanitization. The text comes from a free-form input and would be shared with other users once persisted.
findings.impact: An attacker can run JavaScript in other users' browsers, enabling session theft and actions performed as the victim.
findings.remediation: Render the text as a normal React text node so it is auto-escaped. If rich text is needed, sanitize it with a library such as DOMPurify using a strict allowlist.

findings.title: Unauthenticated get-profile with service-role key allows reading any profile (IDOR)
findings.description: The caller-supplied userId selects a profile with the RLS-bypassing service-role key. There is no authentication, and no check that the caller owns the profile. `select("*")` returns all columns.
findings.impact: An attacker can enumerate or read any user's profile data, including role and bio.
findings.remediation: Authenticate the caller via JWT and use their user id, or use a user-scoped client so RLS applies. Select only the needed columns and validate the UUID format.

related.note: Error details are returned via String(error)

findings.title: Profile update policy allows users to change their own role (privilege escalation)
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can update own profile"
ON public.profiles
FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (id = auth.uid())
WITH CHECK (id = auth.uid());
findings.description: The policy restricts rows but not columns. A user can update their own row, including the `role` column, to 'admin'.
findings.impact: Any authenticated user can grant themselves admin rights.
findings.remediation: Prevent role changes with a WITH CHECK that compares against the existing role, or revoke column UPDATE privileges and grant only safe columns. A BEFORE UPDATE trigger is another option.
findings.validation_notes: Confirm that the roles table or app logic does not rely on profiles.role for admin checks elsewhere.

findings.title: RLS policy lets any authenticated user read all tasks
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (true);
findings.description: The SELECT policy on tasks is always true, so every authenticated user can read every task. This is inconsistent with the owner-based update and projects policies.
findings.impact: Users can read other users' private task titles and descriptions.
findings.remediation: Restrict reads to the owner, or to project members.
findings.secure_code:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (owner_id = auth.uid());

related.note: The comments policy depends on the tasks table. Its EXISTS subquery does not filter by owner, so it is still effectively open unless the tasks policy is restricted.

findings.title: Tasks insert/update policies do not protect project_id (cross-project injection)
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can create tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR INSERT
TO authenticated
WITH CHECK (owner_id = auth.uid());

CREATE POLICY "Users can update tasks"
ON public.tasks
FOR UPDATE
TO authenticated
USING (owner_id = auth.uid())
findings.description: The policies check only owner_id. A user can insert tasks into, or move tasks to, any project_id, including projects they do not own.
findings.impact: Users can inject or move tasks into other users' projects, polluting or tampering with them.
findings.remediation: Require in WITH CHECK that the referenced project belongs to the user, or that the user is a member of it. Restrict updates to the project_id column.

related.note: Comment insert lacks a task access check

findings.title: task_comments policies do not tie access to task ownership
findings.description: The SELECT sub-query is true for any existing task, so every comment is readable by any authenticated user. The INSERT policy checks only author_id, so users can comment on any task_id.
findings.impact: Users can read comments on private tasks and post comments on tasks they have no access to.
findings.remediation: Make the sub-query check that the caller can access the parent task (owner or project owner) in both SELECT and INSERT.

findings.title: Hardcoded credential-like analytics key in source
findings.description: A credential-like API key is hardcoded in client source. The value is placeholder-like and located in demo config.
findings.impact: If it is a real key, it would be exposed to anyone with the bundle.
findings.remediation: Confirm it is a non-production or public write key. Otherwise load it from build-time environment variables and rotate it.
findings.validation_notes: Confirm that this is a placeholder or a public analytics write key, not a production secret.

findings.title: Wildcard CORS on a state-changing endpoint
findings.description: The write endpoint allows any origin to call it from the browser.
findings.impact: Any website can invoke the endpoint. Combined with the missing authentication, this makes cross-origin abuse trivial.
findings.remediation: Restrict the allowed origin to the known front-end origin(s) and require authentication.
findings.validation_notes: Impact is limited if JWT auth is added, since no cookies are used.

findings.title: Verbose error details leaked to client
findings.description: The raw database/exception error is returned to the caller.
findings.impact: Reveals schema, constraint and internal details that help an attacker refine attacks.
findings.remediation: Log errors server-side and return a generic message.
findings.secure_code:
console.error("update-task failed:", error);
return Response.json({ error: "Unable to update task" }, { status: 500, headers: corsHeaders });

findings.title: Profiles readable by all authenticated users (all columns)
findings.evidence:
CREATE POLICY "Users can view profiles"
ON public.profiles
FOR SELECT
TO authenticated
USING (true);
findings.description: Every authenticated user can read every profile row, including role and bio.
findings.impact: User enumeration and exposure of role information.
findings.remediation: Limit to own row, or expose a view with only the public columns.
findings.validation_notes: This may be intended if profiles are public within the app.
